claims.text: In terms of raw volume, New York City had the highest number of gentrified tracts (128), despite a lower percentage share (29.8%) due to its large total tract count [Source: ev-2].

claims.text: While cities generally became wealthier in nominal terms since 1980, this prosperity was unevenly distributed [Source: ev-1].
New York City led with a Gini coefficient of 0.5469, while Atlanta and Miami recorded coefficients of 0.57, and New Orleans reached 0.56 [Source: ev-1].
Several metros showed extreme patterns with Gini coefficients exceeding 0.54 and income ratios reaching 18:1 between top and bottom earners [Source: ev-1].
Specific income ratio analyses confirm this widening gap [Source: ev-1].
By 2018–2021, Federal Reserve data tracking over 3,140 series confirmed that U.S. [Source: ev-1]
inequality reached record levels, showing the sharpest increase among advanced economies since the 1980s [Source: ev-1].
The relationship between income growth and housing costs has deteriorated significantly regarding affordability and economic mobility [Source: ev-1].
This disparity is most acute on the West Coast; California cities exhibit price-to-income ratios between 9.6 and 12.2, more than double the national average of 4.7 [Source: ev-1].

claims.text: Gentrification has driven distinct demographic changes and displacement patterns [Source: ev-1].

Gentrifying neighborhoods saw population increases (averaging +6.5%) and became whiter, with the non-Hispanic white share increasing by an average of 4.3 percentage points [Source: ev-2] [Source: ev-1].

claims.text: Displacement is not uniform across racial lines [Source: ev-1].

Research indicates that residents from historically Black gentrifying neighborhoods tend to move to poorer non-gentrifying areas, while residents from other gentrifying neighborhoods move to wealthier areas, suggesting minority communities face greater challenges during these transitions [Source: ev-1].
The four-decade transformation was fueled by a shift away from manufacturing toward service industries as structural economic shifts occurred [Source: ev-1].

Since 1980, nearly 80% of the country's population growth among those under 45 was concentrated in metro areas with over 1 million residents, as urban counties gained prime-age workers (ages 25–54) while rural counties lost them [Source: ev-1].
